items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: They had a way of -- like Josephine Baker (unintelligible). She had something. You understand? The way of being outstanding -- getting most of the attention while the performance goes on, see.

ctx.x: But that was the most thrilling thing, see. I mean, of course, now my partner, Chuckles -- like he had to learn these -- he was playing this musical instrument and I think Mr. Ellington -- he was kind of proud of that -- of course, the vibraphone was something like the piano, in a way, you know. And he could (unintelligible) scat operatic, you see. Operatic singing, but he was doing it in scat. And he was very funny -- it was comical. They had him doing this jazz so you -- it just got to be loved -- this fellow,…
to be impressive to him, you know. I guess he was tickled about it, you know. It was a great experience, you see, and he always inspired everyone that I know, especially that show, you see.

Well, I think we got held over there, you see. We got held over at this place, see. That's the Penn Theater, see. Now, that's the first experience that I ever had of being held over. Even with Buck and Bubbles, I mean, we wasn't like in no held-over shows, but we had been in the -- you know, like doubling-- like you'd work in one theater and have to go out of that theater and have to go to the other theater and work. They call that doubling, see. Our repeat performance -- because in one city if the same act is…
